I’ll trace both invite flows and the server-side batch handling, then add inline membership validation and make the batch reject atomically. I’ll inspect the relevant frontend and API conventions first; I won’t install dependencies or run the test suite.
I found a shared organization-invites API plus distinct onboarding and settings logic, which is the right seam for a consistent fix. I’m applying the frontend component/logic and API validation guidance before editing.
The API already validates rows before the bulk save, except the membership check was incorrectly deferred to `create()`. I’ll move that check into field validation so the whole batch is rejected before any side effect. On the client, the existing member store can supply a live, case-insensitive row error in both shared invite surfaces.
The change now validates membership during serializer validation, before a bulk save begins, and the client derives per-row errors from the organization member list plus the current user. I also marked the specific expected 400 response as non-reportable, while keeping genuine API failures reportable.
Implemented.

- Invite rows now flag invalid addresses and emails already belonging to the organization, including the current user, in both onboarding and organization settings.
- Bulk invites validate membership before saving, so an existing member in any row prevents all invites and emails.
- Added a dedicated validation code and excluded that expected 400 from error tracking.
- Added coverage for a bulk request containing the current member email.

I did not install dependencies or run the test suite, per your request.
